comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Bank of America disclose specific credit quality metrics for their Commercial Real Estate (CRE) portfolios. Citigroup reports the Allowance for Credit Losses (ACLL) rate (1.60%) and non-accrual CRE loan amounts ($574 million) as of year-end 2024. Bank of America discloses the volume of 'reservable criticized exposure' for the specific office property type ($5.1 billion) and its aggregate loan-to-value ratio (85%). While Citi provides a broad portfolio ACLL and non-accrual metric, BAC drills down into criticized exposure for a key risk segment (office), illustrating different granularity in reporting CRE credit health.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024, the ACLL attributed to the total funded CRE exposure (including Wealth) was approximately 1.60%, and there were $574 million of non-accrual CRE loans.

Reservable criticized exposure for the office property type was $5.1 billion at December 31, 2024, representing a decrease of $398 million, or seven percent, from December 31, 2023, with an aggregate loan-to-value of approximately 85 percent based on property appraisals completed in the last twelve months.
